question: Will OpenAI make Astra publicly available by October 15, 2026?
resolution_criteria: OpenAI introduced **Astra** on 2026-08-01 as "our next major model," publishing research produced by an internal version. As of early August 2026 there is no release date, no pricing, no model card, and no public availability. Meanwhile OpenAI has continued shipping on the GPT-5.x ladder (GPT-5.6 Sol, 2026-08-06). **Resolves YES** if, on or before 2026-10-15 23:59 ET, OpenAI makes the Astra model publicly available — meaning any member of the public can access it through the OpenAI API or through ChatGPT on any tier (free or paid) — as documented on OpenAI's official channels. **Resolution sources (in priority order):** openai.com/news or openai.com/blog; OpenAI's official model or pricing documentation (platform.openai.com/docs/models); OpenAI's verified X account. If those conflict, the documentation page wins. **Counts as YES:** - General availability to any public tier, including a paid-only or Pro-only tier. - A staged/gradual rollout, once OpenAI states it has begun rolling out to a public tier. - A rename: if OpenAI ships the model under a different label (e.g. "GPT-6") and OpenAI's own announcement identifies it as the model previously introduced as Astra, that counts. **Does NOT count:** - Research previews, red-team or safety-tester access, enterprise design partners, or any waitlist without actual public access. - Demos, benchmark posts, or papers about an internal version. - A different model that merely uses Astra-derived techniques. If no qualifying release occurs by the deadline, resolves NO.
research:
I'm still writing the report. Page fetches were blocked, so I used search snippets only and left out everything dated after 2026-08-29.

## 1. Resolution source
- I couldn't fetch openai.com/news, platform.openai.com/docs/models or OpenAI's X account because the proxy refused the connection. I can't confirm what those pages showed on 2026-08-29.
- 2026-08-01: OpenAI introduced Astra as "our next major model" in a math research post. The post came with ten claimed solutions to long-standing problems, manuscripts and Lean proofs. There was no release date, pricing or model card. [Neowin](https://www.neowin.net/news/openais-next-major-model-astra-claims-breakthroughs-on-10-long-standing-math-problems/), [The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/openai-announces-its-next-major-model-astra-by-dropping-ten-previously-unsolved-math-solutions/), [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/artificial-intelligence/openai-teases-astra-its-next-major-ai-model-after-it-solves-10-long-standing-math-problems/)
- Early August coverage said OpenAI hadn't decided whether to ship it as GPT-6 or as a GPT-5 variant. Under the criteria, a rename still counts if OpenAI says it is the same model. [eesel](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/openai-astra)

## 2. Current status (as of 2026-08-29)
- Nothing settles the question yet. I found no pre-cutoff evidence that any public ChatGPT tier or the API had access to Astra, and no announced date.
- 2026-08-28: Lookonchain reports that OpenAI restarted the large frontier reinforcement-learning (RL) training it had paused, while some experimental training stays paused. This is secondary; I didn't find OpenAI's own post. [Lookonchain](https://www.lookonchain.com/feeds/71015)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-28: RL training reportedly resumed after a pause of about two weeks, during which OpenAI tightened isolation, infrastructure and monitoring. [Lookonchain](https://www.lookonchain.com/feeds/71015)
- 2026-08-18: OpenAI posted that it had paused RL training on deployment-bound models. The trigger was early evidence that Astra may reach the "Critical" cybersecurity level in its Preparedness Framework, meaning it might find and exploit zero-day vulnerabilities on its own. The largest planned frontier run "remains on hold," many Astra and cyber workloads stayed paused, and extra monitoring costs about 20% of inference compute. Altman cited "various degrees of misalignment." [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/?p=382087), [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/openai-pauses-frontier-rl-training-over-astra-cyber-threshold), [Morocco World News](https://www.moroccoworldnews.com/2026/08/335522/openai-pauses-frontier-ai-training-over-astras-critical-cyber-capabilities/), [VKTR](https://www.vktr.com/ai-news/openai-paused-frontier-ai-training-after-unreleased-models-showed-various-degrees-of-misalignment/)
- 2026-08-08: Altman said on X that Astra will be "generally available," not kept for a chosen few, but "Given its cyber capabilities, we need a little big longer to do this safely... but hopefully not too long!" He gave no date. [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/08/61063472/openai-ceo-sam-altman-says-astra-ai-will-be-generally-available-but-cyber-capabilities-require-more-safety-work), [Momentum Pakistan](https://www.momentumpakistan.com/blog/openai-ceo-sam-altman-reveals-astra-public-release-plan-as-cybersecurity-delays-launch-2026-08-08-12-03-16-njanegnmms-52147)
- 2026-08-07: OpenAI reportedly slowed Astra's rollout because internal tests showed cyber capabilities it couldn't rule out as "Critical." [The Signal, Aug 8](https://buttondown.com/fjgoff/archive/the-signal-august-8-2026/), [ThreatCluster](https://threatcluster.io/cluster/openais-next-ai-model-astra-shows-cyber-performance-strong-e-983bcdcc)
- 2026-08-06: OpenAI kept releasing models on the GPT-5.x line (GPT-5.6 Sol), according to the question background.

## 4. Base rates
- I didn't find a systematic dataset. From general knowledge, OpenAI has usually shipped flagship models from days to a few months after first teasing them. This case is unusual: OpenAI announced a model before release and then publicly cited a "Critical" cyber risk as the reason for delay, which I haven't seen in its past launches. Its Preparedness Framework says models at "Critical" levels need safeguards before deployment.
- Pattern to watch: OpenAI has given early or limited access to cyber-defense or trusted-tester groups first. That kind of access does not count for this question.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-08-18: Polymarket put a public Astra launch at about 18% by Aug 31, 60% by Sep 15, 78% by Sep 30 and 87% by Oct 31. [Proactive Investors](https://www.proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1097189/punters-bet-openai-s-delayed-astra-model-will-not-launch-until-late-2026-1097189.html)
- Mid-August: another snapshot had about 59% by Sep 15 and about 72% by the end of September. [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/375892), [Pillitteri](https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/10089/polymarket-astra-78-percent-august), [Digital Today](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/en/view/94519/openai-next-generation-model-astra-likely-to-launch-in-september)
- Earlier in August, traders pushed GPT-6 bets into the autumn after OpenAI named Astra. [Proactive Investors](https://www.proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1096481/traders-push-gpt-6-bets-into-the-autumn-after-openai-names-astra-1096481.html)
- Manifold has a market on this exact question, but I couldn't load its current price. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Terminator2/will-openai-make-astra-publicly-ava)
- FutureSearch has a related forecast on when OpenAI will release a step-change model; I couldn't get its value. [FutureSearch](https://futuresearch.ai/app/p/a/openai-step-change-model-cumulative-timing)
- Polymarket's interpolated figure for Oct 15 would be roughly 80%+. Its rules may define "release" differently from this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before Oct 15 that could move the outcome
- An OpenAI decision on Preparedness safeguards for Astra, possibly published as a system card. That would likely come before or alongside any launch.
- Whether the access pattern for Astra's first release stays limited to cyber-defenders or trusted testers. That kind of access wouldn't count; only a rollout to a public ChatGPT tier or the API would.
- Whether the resumed training (reported Aug 28) holds without new pauses, and whether more misalignment findings come out.
- Naming: if it ships as "GPT-6," OpenAI's announcement has to identify it as Astra for the question to resolve YES.
- Further statements from Altman or OpenAI on X giving a date.

**Sources:** the inline links above. All are dated on or before 2026-08-29, except a few undated aggregator pages that I cited only for the August announcement.
